focus: Frontier node F-2-009 (depth 2, scope OpenBot-main/app/src/components/memory, OpenBot-main/docs, .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots): How should shared versus per-person memory be scoped when a few people use the same bots, and what does OpenBot's memory model do that skilled bots' per-bot files do not?
noveltyJustification: Eight findings are new evidence from OpenBot's memory and learning docs, the BOT.md schema, the runtime module table and two other repos' memory models; two are design inferences.

graphEvents.label: OpenBot memory is team-only and provenance-gated
Skilled bots runtime has no memory module

label: OpenBot's personal memory exists only in the team edition; the personal edition has none because local Intelligence is licensed without memory.
OpenBot shares person-added facts with all of that person's bots, while facts a bot picks up stay with that bot.

OpenBot keeps memory provenance (origin, review state, forming bot, importing source) and applies it before a bot sees anything; bot-formed memory reaches only the forming bot while it holds the source app, and project-scoped results are dropped.

Skills-from-use is a separate learning loop: completed conversations feed a Learning container, Intelligence proposes skills with SKILL.md and evidence, and a person approves or rejects; the team edition never auto-approves.
Learning containers are per person: a run draws the bot's skills first, then the person's, then skills another person opened, and each person chooses sharing scope.
Skilled bots' BOT.md schema has no memory field: id, trigger, runtime, budget, enabled, delivery, posture, precheck, specFolder and body.
The bots runtime has 28 flat modules and none is memory; memory is not a runtime concern today.

Turnstone's structured memory is the cleanest small model: four types, five scopes, identity tuple of name/scope/scope id, upsert on the same identity, and a body-free metadata index with explicit get.
Openhuman's memory is service-shaped: recall, fetch and store over a pluggable engine in CortexDB, and off entirely without an engine.

Smallest change is typed memory files: per-bot bots/<id>/memory.md and shared bots/memory.md, entries typed user/general/feedback/reference with actor, source, bot and date, appended by bots remember and prepended to the prompt; learned skills stay a proposed SKILL.md reviewed in a packet.

direction: Building a memory service or embedding store
reason: Service-shaped memories exist to serve many users and machines; a few people on one host do not need recall ranking.
They depend on a hosted backend and a skills marketplace; a proposed SKILL.md reviewed in a packet gives the same value.

direction: Giving each bot its own memory schema
reason: The BOT.md contract is already small and stable; memory belongs beside the bot, not inside its definition.
